I have been asked by Defendants to review materials pertaining to, and to formulate opinions, regarding Ms. Moller’s kratom use. 2. My time spent in the preparation of this opinion letter and reviewing documents to formulate my opinions, as well as for any deposition or trial testimony I may be called upon to give, will be billed at a rate of $725 per hour. My opinions in this matter are expressed to a reasonable degree of scientific certainty and are based on information available to me on the date of this report. I have provided a list of documents that were reviewed in forming my opinions. This report may be supplemented if new information becomes available. 3. My opinions below are based on my background, education, training, experience, and the information available to me as of the date of this report. I reserve the right to amend or supplement my opinions to the extent that new information becomes available. 4. My opinions are also based on information that is related to this case, which includes a review of case materials provided to me by counsel, documents in the open scientific literature, and the opinions of some other experts. 5. A copy of my current curriculum vitae is attached as Appendix A. My list of References and Documents Considered is attached as Appendix B. My list of prior testimony for the last four years is set out in Appendix C. EXPERIENCE 6. I am a board-certified toxicologist and certified industrial hygienist with nearly 40 years of experience in occupational health, risk assessment, toxicology, and environmental engineering. My experience includes investigating the health effects of exposure to, as well as the remediation of, carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic chemicals, including dioxins, furans, benzenes, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), petroleum products, methyl tertiary-butyl ether (MTBE), chlorinated hydrocarbons, glycol ethers, beryllium, lead, 1,3-butadiene, methylene chloride, tetrachloroethylene (PCE), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), chromium, MCHM, airborne biologic agents, kratom and kava, nicotine and asbestos, to name a few. I have published about 300 peer- 1

Case 2:24-cv-00228-WBV-DPC Document 253-16 Filed 03/02/26 Page 16 of 18 OVERVIEW OF MY OPINIONS Opinion 1 - People in numerous countries have used kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) safely for hundreds (if not thousands) of years. The body of scientific literature on kratom and its alkaloids continues to evolve, but historic and recent data indicate that beneficial effects associated with kratom use have a robust pharmacologic basis. It is my opinion that few to no adverse effects are expected in typical users when kratom is used alone and that adverse outcomes in dual- and polysubstance users can be attributed to other compounds, not kratom or its alkaloids. Opinion 2 - The risk assessment process is a methodology that is widely accepted and used by many scientific bodies and governmental agencies around the world. It is my opinion that it is an appropriate method to use for characterizing the health risks potentially associated with use of kratom products (especially when comparing potential health risks associated with kratom use to those associated with use of opioids to yield similar effects). Opinion 3 - The health effects of kratom can be attributed to more than 50 indole alkaloids present in the plant. Of these, mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine are the most biologically significant. It is my opinion that alkaloid concentrations vary across kratom product types, but data from the peer-reviewed literature indicates that these typical concentrations contained in teas or capsules, taken in a reasonable manner, would not increase the risk of acute or chronic adverse health effects among typical users. Opinion 4 - Animal studies and studies of humans are defined as in vivo analyses. Kratom, mitragynine, 7-hydroxymitragynine, and other associated alkaloids have been studied in vivo for over 100 years. It is my opinion that these studies provide support for two primary conclusions. First, kratom and its alkaloids can yield dose-dependent stimulant or pain relief effects under typical human use and may aid with opioid withdrawal. Second, kratom alkaloids can be classified as very low to moderately toxic in animals. It is my opinion that since these alkaloids are only a small percentage of kratom products by weight, few to no adverse health effects are expected in kratom users, even among higher volume consumers. No chronic adverse 13

Case 2:24-cv-00228-WBV-DPC Document 253-16 Filed 03/02/26 Page 17 of 18 effects have been reported in vivo following repeated kratom administration at relatively high doses to test animals or humans. Opinion 5 - Studies of isolated cells, termed in vitro analyses, help provide information on potential organ-specific effects and the toxicological mechanisms driving health outcomes following exposure to a given compound. In vitro data indicate that kratom alkaloids are primarily metabolized by Cytochrome P450 (CYP) isoforms CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 and that physiological effects are driven by alkaloid activity at opioid, adrenergic, serotonergic, and dopaminergic receptors. Kratom’s pain relief (analgesic) and euphoric effects can be explained by kratom alkaloid binding at opioid receptors (ORs). However, it is my opinion that the activity of mitragynine, 7-hydroxymitragynine, and other kratom alkaloids at ORs is weak relative to that of numerous drugs (e.g., morphine, fentanyl) and endogenous endorphins (e.g., β-endorphin, enkephalins, dynorphins). However, depending on the dose, 7-hydroxymitragynine can cause morphine like effects if ingested in a relatively pure state (i.e., as a synthetic isolate). Opinion 6 - Data on the effects of kratom use in humans includes epidemiological evidence, as well as information from case reports and case series. Case data indicate that kratom’s alkaloids produce few to no acute adverse health effects when kratom is used alone, but that mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine have been reported along with other compounds in the post-mortem blood and tissues of dual- and polysubstance users. BASES FOR OPINIONS Basis of Opinion 1 M. Speciosa Traditional Use 47. Mitragyna speciosa, commonly known as kratom, is a tree native to Southeast Asia, specifically, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Borneo, Myanmar, and Vietnam. M. speciosa can reach up to 25 meters tall at maturity and is noted for having dark green leaves with green, white, or red veins (Cinosi et al. 2015). It conventionally grows in swampy areas, in areas inundated by water, and alongside riverbanks (Grundmann 2017; Ahmad et al. 2022). Depending on the country, kratom is referred to by its local name: ketum or biak (Malaysia), keton or kadamba (Indonesia), benisa (Myanmar), mambog or lugub (Philippines), ithang, thom, kratom (Thailand), or giam (Vietnam) (Gong et al. 2012; Cinosi et al. 2015; Grundmann 2017; Eastlack et al. 2020). 48. Kratom leaves were historically used in rural communities by farmers, laborers, or fishermen in Southeast Asia as a stimulant to reduce or prevent fatigue stemming from hard labor by chewing the leaves raw or drying them for later consumption (Cinosi et al. 2015; Grundmann 2017; Singh et al. 2017).
